designation: IN THE COURT OF DISTRICT & SESSIONS JUDGE
jurisdictionNote: District-level criminal and civil courts in Arunachal Pradesh, supervised by the Gauhati High Court — Itanagar Permanent Bench. Arunachal Pradesh has 25 districts (post-2020 reorganisations carving out Kamle, Lepa Rada, Shi Yomi, Pakke Kessang and others). English is the State and judicial working language under the Arunachal Pradesh Official Language Act, 2007. The Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945 and the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873 (Inner Line) historically governed administration; tribal customary law and Gaon Bura / Kebang councils retain significant role in civil and family matters.

party_designation.state: State of Arunachal Pradesh through the Principal Secretary, Home Department, Government of Arunachal Pradesh, Itanagar

verification_format:
I, {deponent_name}, {designation}, do hereby solemnly verify and declare that the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ of the above petition are true to my personal knowledge and the contents of paragraphs ___ to ___ are based on information received and legal advice tendered, which I believe to be true. Nothing material has been concealed therefrom.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

DEPONENT
localRules: English is the sole official language of pleadings before the subordinate judiciary in Arunachal Pradesh.
Bail applications under S.483 BNSS (formerly S.439 CrPC) must disclose prior rejections and be accompanied by certified copy of the FIR.
Anticipatory bail applications (S.482 BNSS) require certified copy of FIR and grounds; the Gauhati HC Itanagar Bench is the preferred forum for serious offences.
Vakalatnama in the form prescribed under the Gauhati High Court Rules with requisite court-fee stamp.
Court-fee under the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as adopted by Arunachal Pradesh.
SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, POCSO and NDPS cases tried by designated Special Courts at the district headquarters.

Arunachal Pradesh continues to apply the Assam Frontier (Administration of Justice) Regulation, 1945 — Deputy Commissioners, Additional DCs and EACs exercise civil and criminal magisterial powers in many districts alongside regular judicial officers; the subordinate judicial cadre has been progressively constituted but advocate must verify whether a regular Sessions/District Court or the DC's court has jurisdiction at the relevant station.

Customary courts — Gaon Bura, Kebang, Buliang, Abala — retain primary jurisdiction over tribal customary matters under Section 5 of the 1945 Regulation; advocate must verify forum jurisdiction before filing matters involving land, inheritance and personal law among tribals.
Inner Line Permit regime under the Bengal Eastern Frontier Regulation, 1873 is operative — affidavits and verification by non-tribal deponents may require declaration of ILP/RP status where relevant.
e_filing_note: e-Filing operational at Itanagar, Naharlagun via eCourts portal; not yet mandatory state-wide.
